title: The Copper Ledger
premise: Orsen Winterbourne, a battlefield nurse in a coastal garrison town, keeps a hidden ledger recording the names of soldiers the officers' official reports omit — the forgotten, the disgraced, the poor. When the army requisitions the town and confiscates her ledger, she is forced to work for the very officers she has quietly documented, and falls in love with Captain Elias Vane, a man whose duty demands the ledger's destruction. As an evacuation ship prepares to sail on the morning tide with only one berth left, Orsen must decide between saving her ailing brother or the orphaned boy whose name exists only in her pages. She gives the berth to the boy, surrenders the ledger to the sea rather than let it be weaponized, and stays behind with Elias — choosing memory kept in people over memory kept in ink, and love against duty at last.
about_author: C. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military hospital records from forgotten coastal towns. Their fiction is drawn to the small, unrecorded lives that official history leaves in the margins.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Orsen, in her own POV, works a feverish night in the garrison infirmary, recording in her hidden copper-clasped ledger the names of dead soldiers the morning report omits. We learn of her brother Tom, her sense that history happens elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet defiance and the comfort of routine.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: The army seizes the town: billets, supplies, and, through a clerk's blunder, Orsen's ledger. Orsen's POV. She watches Major Halloway's men carry off her copper-clasped book and realizes every name she protected is now evidence. Emotional beat: violation and dawning fear.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Captain Elias Vane, tasked with assessing the ledger's contents, summons Orsen to interpret her shorthand. His POV. He expects a crank or a spy; instead he finds a woman who remembers what his superiors erase. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination, the first crack in his loyalty.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Halloway offers a bargain: her cooperation in exchange for the ledger's quiet return — and Tom's exemption from the next embarkation. Orsen accepts, hating the leash. Elias witnesses the deal and says nothing. Emotional beat: complicity, the first compromise of her principles.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Elias and Orsen walk the emptied harbor at dusk; he confesses he once falsified a casualty report to spare a widow, and she tells him about the boy Wren, an orphan whose name lives only in her pages. His POV. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared guilt.

chapters.title: The Evacuation Order
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orders arrive: the town will be abandoned, one ship, limited berths, families ranked by usefulness. Tom's exemption is revoked — Halloway's bargain was a lie. Orsen discovers Wren is not on any list at all. Emotional beat: betrayal and cold clarity.

chapters.title: Halloway's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Halloway orders the ledger burned and instructs Elias to ensure 'surplus persons' — the unlisted — are left behind. Elias copies the ledger by lamplight, a treasonous act of memory. Emotional beat: the moment duty and conscience become irreconcilable.

chapters.title: One Berth
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, night before the tide. Through Elias she secures a single extra berth — one name only. Tom begs her not to choose the boy; Wren clutches her sleeve and recites the names from the ledger like a prayer. Emotional beat: the impossible arithmetic of love.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating between both POVs in quick cuts. At the gangway, Orsen gives the berth to Wren; Tom, furious and heartbroken, boards alone. Halloway discovers the copied ledger; Elias claims it as his own doing. Orsen throws the original into the sea. Emotional beat: sacrifice made irrevocable.

chapters.title: Names Kept in People
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, weeks later. The town is rubble; she and Elias, both stripped of rank, remain as caretakers of a mass grave. Wren's letter arrives from across the water, reciting the names back to her — the ledger now living in him. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose, love chosen over duty.
